info.title: Nex Controller and Core API
info.description: Implemented development API for administrator inventory, enrollment, durable operations, appliance adoption and managed-VM creation. Capability-gated storage/network registration, bounded ISO transfer and stopped-VM provisioning use outbound authenticated Core reports. Browser VM consoles use single-use tickets, an outbound host tunnel and a same-origin WebSocket. Central VM power requests (start, shutdown, reboot, force-stop) are durable host operations.

get.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Read-only; safe to retry. Returns CSRF token for same-origin mutations. All authenticated administrator operations have controller-wide scope. Does not extend the idle deadline. A 401 requires sign-in again; session JSON fields are unchanged and contain no expiry timestamps.

401.description: Missing, expired, invalid, or revoked credentials.

post.description: Validates existing administrator credentials and browser origin. Sets __Host-nex_session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and no Domain. Each login creates a new session; at most 64 active sessions per service. Sessions expire after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation and eight hours absolutely; GET/HEAD polling does not renew them. Legacy unprefixed cookies are not accepted; sign in again after upgrade. Existing password hashes remain valid; new administrator bootstrap passwords must be nonempty valid UTF-8, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, without CR, LF or NUL; there is no minimum length or complexity rule. Login admission permits at most five valid-length attempts per one-minute actual peer-IP window, two concurrent password checks per service, and 4096 tracked peers. Forwarded client-IP headers are ignored. Login returns 429 when rate/concurrency/table or 64-session capacity is exhausted; bounded retries must not create an unbounded loop.

No Retry-After header is emitted because concurrency saturation has no fixed expiry.

post.summary: Probe a host's local API TLS certificate
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Performs an insecure TLS 1.3 handshake to the given address (default port 9443) purely to capture the leaf certificate nex-core-local presents; it establishes no trust and stores nothing. The operator compares the returned fingerprint, subject and expiry against the physical host before confirming add-host. This never contacts the Controller-to-Core enrollment contract; it only inspects the host's existing local API listener.

post.summary: Add a host by address and root password
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Replaces manual token enrollment for a reachable host: the operator first confirms the certificate fingerprint returned by probeHost, then submits it here alongside the host's root password. The Controller re-verifies that same fingerprint with a constant-time comparison during its own outbound TLS handshake to the host — a mismatch fails the handshake and returns 502 before the password is ever sent. On a verified connection the Controller signs in to the host's local API (POST /api/local/v1/session), mints a fresh site-bound enrollment token (the same token contract createEnrollmentToken uses), and pushes it to the host's local enrollment endpoint together with the Controller's own served HTTPS certificate (the -tls-cert file, not the host-identity CA) as the trust the host pins for its Controller connection; the host then enrolls with this Controller through the existing agent-enrollment contract and becomes the master of a new pool in this site. The root password is used once for that single sign-in and is never stored, logged, or echoed back, including in error messages. Unknown site_id returns 400. Optional host_id re-enrolls a revoked host whose pool belongs to this site (409 otherwise, checked before any network attempt). A wrong password returns 401; a login rate limit returns 429 with the host's own message. If the host reports it is already enrolled under a different identity, this returns 409 with that host_id — retrying the same add-host call after a lost response is safe and resolves the same way: fetch inventory to see the enrolled host. Any other host-side failure returns 502 naming the controller_url the host was asked to reach, and any token minted for the attempt is deleted. If the Controller process has no served certificate configured, 503 is returned before any host contact; use manual enrollment.

Persist a stable request_id before sending; retry the same host/kind/request_id to recover the same durable operation. Poll operations for completion. Conflicting active work is serialized. post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Outbound HTTPS; agent must verify Controller identity before transmitting its site-bound token. Provide a signed PEM ECDSA P-256 CSR and nonblank hostname (maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL). A fresh enrollment creates a pool in the token site, named after the request hostname, with this host as its master, then records the host in that pool in the same transaction (audit pool.create and host.enroll). Re-enrollment keeps the existing host and pool. Issues a 90-day host-specific client certificate and CA. The token binds to its first CSR; an identical token/CSR retry before token expiry returns the same identity without duplicate enrollment. A different CSR returns 409. After expiry or revocation obtain a new site-bound token; replacement requires explicit revoked host selection. Enrollment has no VM side effects.

post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Outbound mutual TLS authenticates exactly one enrolled, unrevoked host. Version must be 1. Persist a strictly increasing sequence across restarts; discard superseded reports. Null/omitted inventory is heartbeat only and never makes old checks healthy. Results refer only to this host operations; acknowledge persisted results before deleting local journal entries. Commands can redeliver and must be reconciled by operation_id. Controller reconnect requires fresh inventory; no automatic VM restart is permitted. Sequence range is 1 through 9223372036854775807. Superseded sequences receive 200 but do not update last-seen or inventory; operation results and command redelivery still reconcile. At most 100 results per report; result error is at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Results for queued, undelivered operations return 409, foreign/unknown operation IDs return 400. Terminal results are acknowledged without rewriting the original outcome. At most 100 pending commands return, in creation order. Inventory fields merge only when inventory observed_at increases; individual checks merge only when their observed_at increases. Controller derives per-check freshness independently from heartbeat freshness. Health changes are recorded as debounced audit transitions (default debounce five seconds, configurable). Reports advertise at most 32 capabilities of up to 100 UTF-8 bytes each. managed-vm-v1 gates new commands; omission prevents managed delivery and a newer sequence clears stored capabilities. Result states include needs_attention for uncertain host effects. Upgrade Controller before Core because older Controllers reject the new fields.

post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Outbound mutual TLS requires the current valid, unrevoked host certificate. CSR binds the next certificate to the same host. Persist identity atomically; retain recovery access on an ambiguous response. No VM side effects. Requires signed PEM ECDSA P-256 CSR. The new certificate lasts 90 days; previous certificates overlap for at most ten minutes. Repeating the same CSR while authenticated returns the existing unexpired certificate. After the overlap expires, use persisted new identity or explicitly revoke and re-enroll.

post.summary: Create initial appliance site and enrollment intent
post.description: Administrator-only appliance bootstrap. Persist a stable request_id and random 64-character lowercase hexadecimal enrollment_token before submission. The same request, names and token return the original site without duplicates. Payload changes conflict. An authenticated replay refreshes token expiry to ten minutes without clearing a consumed token's CSR binding; consumed tokens support replay only of the already-enrolled agent CSR through the existing enrollment endpoint. No pool is created here: the appliance host becomes the master of an automatic pool when it enrolls. This does not create or start a VM. Core enrollment remains outbound verified HTTPS protocol v1. Revoked enrollment tokens are not recreated; use explicit recovery.

post.summary: Upload and transfer a guest ISO
post.description: Administrator session required. Mutations require same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token; JSON rejects unknown fields and bodies over 1 MiB. Persist request_id before sending. Identical payload replays return the same resource/operation; changed payload conflicts. New work requires a fresh active host in the selected pool advertising managed-vm-v1. Poll resource lists and operations for terminal results. HTTP acceptance is not host completion. Send the raw ISO body, not multipart or JSON. Name must be a basename ending .iso. Controller hashes the actual stream, verifies CD001 at offset 32769 and stages privately before committing an iso-import command. Maximum 8 GiB per image, 16 GiB total staging, 256 MiB free-space reserve; one transfer admission at a time, 2-hour read/write budget. Capacity is bounded even with absent/false Content-Length. Identical retries reupload and hash the bytes before comparing the original request. Terminal import results release Controller staging; orphan files are removed at startup. No remote URL fetch or public media download.

post.summary: Issue a single-use console ticket for a running VM
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token, and an empty JSON object body. The VM must be an adopted appliance or a successfully created guest, its assigned host must be freshly connected, unrevoked and report capability console-v1, and the VM must be observed running in fresh libvirt inventory. The ticket is bound to the requesting session user and VM, lives 60 seconds in Controller memory only, is delivered once to the host in its next report response and is consumed by the first matching WebSocket. The action is audited as console.open. No power operation is implied; a Controller restart ends open consoles without affecting the guest.

get.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0. WebSocket upgrade (RFC 6455, binary frames carrying raw RFB/VNC bytes for noVNC) authenticated by the administrator session cookie; the Origin header must equal the Controller origin and the ticket must be unconsumed, unexpired and issued to this session user for this VM. Controller waits up to 20 seconds for the host's outbound tunnel, then relays bytes both ways until either side closes. HTTP/1.1 is negotiated for this route; no other transport is offered. The ticket is consumed on first use.

post.summary: Attach the host's outbound console tunnel
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Core sends this over its enrolled, hostname-verified mTLS connection with Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: nex-console after receiving a console request in a report response and dialing the running VM's local VNC UNIX socket. The token must name an unexpired session for this exact host that has no tunnel yet. The response is 101 and the connection then carries raw VNC bytes both ways until the browser or VM side closes. Other hosts, unknown or expired tokens and duplicate tunnels receive 404. No browser session or CSRF token is used on this agent route; Core never listens for inbound console connections.

post.summary: Request a VM power action on its assigned host
post.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0, protocol v1. Requires an administrator session, same Origin and X-CSRF-Token. Persist request_id before sending; the same id replays the same durable operation, a different action under the same id is 409. The VM must be an adopted appliance or a successfully created guest; its assigned host must be freshly connected, unrevoked and report managed-vm-v1 and vm-power-v1, and at most one power request per VM may be queued or dispatched. The request is audited as vm-power and delivered to the host in its next report; poll operations for the result. A succeeded shutdown or reboot means the ACPI request was issued, not that the guest honored it: the VM's observed state is the truth. Controller outage never stops a guest.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: VM UUID.

200.description: Replay of an existing request_id with the same VM and action.

400.description: Malformed JSON, unknown field, invalid request_id or unsupported action.

401.description: Missing, expired, invalid, or revoked credentials.

403.description: Authorization, origin, or CSRF validation failed.

409.description: Host not fresh, revoked, outside the pool or without vm-power-v1; request_id reused with different input; or another power request for this VM is pending.

500.description: Controller persistence or internal failure.

AdminSession.name: __Host-nex_session
AdminSession.description: Administrator session cookie __Host-nex_session, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict, Path=/ with no Domain. Expires after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation or eight hours absolutely. GET/HEAD polling does not extend idle lifetime; mutations also require matching Origin and X-CSRF-Token. At most 64 active sessions per service. Legacy unprefixed cookies are refused; sign in again after upgrading.

x-session-policy.idle_refresh: authenticated mutations after Origin/CSRF validation; GET and HEAD never extend it

HostCertificate.description: Unique signed host certificate; current enrollment and revocation are checked on each request.

master_host_id.description: Host that controls this pool. Empty only for databases migrated from the removed manual pool creation with no host.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

error.description: Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes; absence means no error detail supplied.

freshness.description: Controller-derived elapsed receipt freshness; agent input is ignored. Never infer a current healthy check solely from fresh host connection.

Check.description: Per-probe health distinct from management connection freshness. observed_at marks the check result; last_success is absent until success is observed; error carries actionable failure details.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

kind.description: Interface classification for uplink selection; absent from older agents.

master.description: Bridge or bond this device is enslaved to; absent when standalone or from older agents.

parent.description: For 802.1Q VLAN devices, the raw device they sit on.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

available_bytes.description: Available filesystem bytes when known; absent for raw block devices or unsupported capacity observations.

id.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR/LF/NUL.

state.description: Observed libvirt state; maximum 100 UTF-8 bytes.

guest.description: Host observation of the running guest through its virtio channels; absent for VMs that are not running and from Core builds that predate guest observation.

os_version.description: PRETTY_NAME from /etc/os-release. On Nex Core this is "Nex Core <version>", the single product version (the nex-core-local package). Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

agent_version.description: nex-core-local package version; equals the Nex Core version on Nex Core hosts. Maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

managed.description: Pool-scoped configuration this host has durably applied, read from the Core managed journal; null or omitted when the host holds nothing. On each managed report Controller adopts, under actor system, every entry it does not hold (request_id adopt-<kind>:<host>:<id>, kind storage-register | network-register | iso-import | vm-create), reusing the resource ID and recording the operation as already succeeded without dispatching a command. Entries that duplicate an existing ID, storage path, network (kind, source) or VM name, and invalid entries, are skipped.

checks.description: At most 256 checks with unique names within a report.

Inventory.description: Read-only host observations; byte quantities are bytes, CPU count is logical CPUs, timestamps are RFC3339 UTC. NIC state describes a local link, not end-to-end reachability. VM state is observed libvirt state, not guest application health. Null lists mean no observations supplied. Controller retains newer inventory resource timestamps and independently newer per-check timestamps; a newer report sequence does not freshen an unchanged or older sample.

connection.description: unknown before any report, fresh within configured stale threshold, stale otherwise, revoked after administrator revocation. Restart cannot establish freshness from persisted wall-clock time alone. Controller default stale threshold is 30 seconds and is configurable; this is not a failure or failover deadline.

last_seen.description: Controller wall-clock receipt time of newest accepted report; null until a report arrives. Freshness is tracked using elapsed time in the active process.

capabilities.description: Last accepted sequenced report capabilities; managed-vm-v1 is required for new managed-VM work. Host connectivity freshness is checked separately.

csr_pem.description: Signed PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST using an ECDSA P-256 key; no trailing PEM data.

hostname.description: Nonblank, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL.

csr_pem.description: Signed PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST using an ECDSA P-256 key; no trailing PEM data.

error.description: At most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; omit for successful checks.

observed_at.description: Agent-reported result time; controller operation updated_at records receipt/commit time. Not proof of guest application health.

inventory.description: Omit or null for heartbeat only; prior inventory remains unchanged and is not made healthy.

capabilities.description: Advertised on every report. managed-vm-v1 enables managed command delivery. Omission or null disables managed delivery for this report; a newer sequence also replaces stored capabilities.

ReportRequest.description: version and sequence are required by runtime validation. results may be omitted or null and defaults to no results. inventory may be omitted or null for heartbeat only.

consoles.description: Console pairings to attach now; omitted when none. Not durable operations: they are delivered once and never journaled.

detail.description: Actionable detail for debounced health transitions when present.

password.description: Existing administrator password, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Existing password hashes remain valid.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL.

host_id.description: Optional revoked host to re-enroll; its pool must belong to site_id.

address.description: Hostname or IP, optionally with :port (default 9443). No scheme, path, or userinfo.

fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters> over the leaf certificate's DER encoding.

subject.description: Leaf certificate subject, for operator confirmation only.

address.description: Hostname or IP, optionally with :port (default 9443). No scheme, path, or userinfo.

fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>, as returned by probeHost and confirmed by the operator.

root_password.description: Used once to sign in to the host's local API; never stored, logged, or echoed. 1-1024 bytes, no NUL.

controller_url.description: This Controller's own HTTPS origin, reachable from the host, given to it as its enrollment target.

host_id.description: Optional revoked host to re-enroll; its pool must belong to this site.

pool_id.description: The automatic pool the enrollment created or, on re-enrollment, kept.

host_id.description: Present when the host reported it is already enrolled.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL.

enrollment_token.description: Caller-generated secret persisted before sending; never log or expose in operation results.

pool_id.description: Optional; when supplied it must equal the host's pool.

vm_id.description: Stable lowercase nonzero libvirt UUID; adoption preserves identity.

guest.description: Latest host guest observation for a VM observed running in a fresh report; omitted otherwise.

ManagedAppliance.description: Unified VM listing. Existing adopted appliances preserve role=controller and protected=true without creation spec/status. Generic guest entries add spec and operation_id/status/error; state/freshness always come from fresh successful libvirt observations independently of creation status.

StorageRegistration.description: Pool registration with explicit access only on host_id; never implies shared storage. status/error reflect its durable operation, not a continuously refreshed filesystem probe. Controller also creates a registration itself (actor system): the default local directory /var/lib/libvirt/images named ISO (request_id auto-storage:<host>), and any storage the host reports in Inventory.managed.storage that Controller does not hold (request_id adopt-storage-register:<host>:<id>, ID and name preserved).

source.description: Bridge name used by guest interfaces (derived <uplink>v<vlan> for kind vlan) or libvirt network name.

uplink.description: Uplink NIC name: required for kind vlan; set on kind bridge when the registration was created automatically for the untagged network of a bridge on a physical port.

NetworkRegistration.description: Pool guest network on one host: an existing bridge, an active libvirt network, or a Core-created VLAN bridge (kind vlan) on an uplink NIC. VLAN bridges are additive; the management bridge, addresses and routes are never changed. Controller also creates registrations itself (actor system): the untagged default network of every host bridge on a physical NIC or bond (request_id auto-network:<host>:<bridge>), and any network the host reports in Inventory.managed.networks that Controller does not hold (request_id adopt-network-register:<host>:<id>, ID and name preserved).

VMCreateSpec.description: Controller-assigned stable UUID and pool membership with separate host assignment. Creation defines a stopped VM, never boots it. Dependencies must be verified on this host/pool; ISO must use selected storage.

path.description: Clean absolute existing non-root local directory, without NUL/CR/LF or symlinks. Core verifies ext4/XFS/Btrfs, free space and write access. Selected directory and all ancestors must be root-owned without group or other write permission. Each directory also requires other-execute permission for QEMU traversal; custom ACL-only paths are unsupported.

source.description: kind bridge/network only: existing bridge or active libvirt network name. Omit for kind vlan; Controller derives the bridge name <uplink>v<vlan>.

uplink.description: kind vlan only: host NIC or bond name that carries the VLAN, at most 10 characters; it must appear in the host inventory as physical or bond (or without a kind from an older agent).

vlan.description: kind vlan only: 802.1Q tag; 0 uses the uplink untagged, which Core refuses when the host has addresses on it.

NetworkRegistrationRequest.description: Exactly one shape: kind bridge/network with source, or kind vlan with uplink and vlan. Mixed fields are rejected with 400.

id.description: Omit; Controller generates the VM UUID.

storage.description: Succeeded storage registrations from the host journal.

networks.description: Succeeded network registrations from the host journal.

media.description: Succeeded ISO imports from the host journal.

vms.description: Succeeded VM definitions from the host journal.

ManagedState.description: Every succeeded registration and VM definition from the Core managed journal, at most 10000 entries per list; each list is omitted when empty. pool_id and host_id inside entries are those of the Controller that created them and are rewritten on adoption; resource IDs are stable across Controllers, which is how a replaced Controller recovers a pool from its master.

token.description: Single-use pairing secret; the host presents it on POST /api/v1/agent/console/{token} within the ticket lifetime.

websocket.description: Same-origin path for the wss:// console stream; carries the ticket.

phase.description: idle, downloading, installing, restarting, done, or failed when an apply is tracked.

progress.description: Percent complete for the current apply when known.

error.description: Non-fatal repo or apply problem; installed_version remains valid for check.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL. Persist before sending; the same id replays the same operation.

interface.description: Guest interface name as reported by the guest agent; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address in CIDR form. Loopback and link-local addresses are omitted.

agent.description: connected: the QEMU guest agent answered; unresponsive: the org.qemu.guest_agent.0 channel is attached but the agent did not answer within 1 second; disconnected: nothing in the guest has opened the channel; no-channel: the VM definition lacks the channel.

os.description: guest-get-osinfo pretty name; absent unless agent is connected. Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

hostname.description: guest-get-host-name; absent unless agent is connected. Maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

addresses.description: guest-network-get-interfaces addresses without loopback or link-local entries; at most 32.

clipboard.description: ready: the guest opened the qemu-vdagent channel (spice-vdagent is running) so the console clipboard works both ways; waiting: the channel exists but nothing in the guest opened it; no-channel: the VM was defined before console clipboard support and must be recreated to gain it.

resize.description: True when the VM has a VirtIO display, so the console can ask the guest to adopt the browser's resolution (needs a virtio-gpu driver in the guest).

GuestInfo.description: Observed inside a running VM by its host through host-local virtio channels: guest agent facts and console channel states. Observation only; a connected agent is not proof of application health.

GET /appliance-ready.json.description: Appliance-only public JSON file served by the existing Controller UI file handler, not a separately registered API route. First boot atomically publishes it after initialization, verified local HTTPS UI HTTP 200, and guest bootstrap-secret cleanup. It must be absent from a pristine appliance image and may return 404 before preparation or on non-appliance deployments. A persisted marker records first-boot completion; it is not continuous health or successful host enrollment/adoption.
GET /appliance-ready.json.compatibility: Host handoff requires bootstrap_version 1, status ready and a successful UI root response over the pinned Controller TLS identity. An older API-only Controller cannot satisfy appliance readiness.

storage-register.semantics: Verify existing local directory access; no formatting. Controller also creates the default ISO registration for /var/lib/libvirt/images (request_id auto-storage:<host>) when absent. Succeeded registrations are reported back in Inventory.managed.storage and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-storage-register:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

network-register.semantics: Verify existing bridge or active libvirt network without edits; for kind vlan, idempotently create bridge <uplink>v<vlan> over the 802.1Q sub-interface, persist it under /etc/network/interfaces.d and refuse uplinks or VLAN devices already used by the host configuration. Succeeded registrations are reported back in Inventory.managed.networks and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-network-register:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

iso-import.semantics: Fetch assigned staged media over host mTLS; verify actual size/hash/ISO before publishing. Succeeded imports are reported back in Inventory.managed.media and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-iso-import:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

vm-create.semantics: Create stopped VM with exclusive new disk; reconcile journal and ownership on replay. Never start a guest. Core resolves storage, network and media references by resource ID, not by pool/host ID, so creation works after re-enrollment under a new Controller. Succeeded definitions are reported back in Inventory.managed.vms and adopted by a Controller that does not hold them (request_id adopt-vm-create:<host>:<id>) without redelivery.

vm-power.semantics: Issue one libvirt start/shutdown/reboot/destroy for the named VM on this host. start and force-stop are idempotent against the observed state; shutdown and reboot are ACPI requests the guest may ignore; paused or transitional states are refused. The stage is journaled before the single request so an interruption is reconciled by observation only: succeeded when the observed state proves the outcome, otherwise needs_attention; never a second request.
